title: Stall remedies and the selfcheck claims check act only on claims the autopilot made, not on another live session's
goal: bl_stall reports a claim-no-commit or returned signal of an item claimed by anyone other than a runner-SP-* of this clone as foreign, with no remedy, and selfcheck's claims check does not fail on it, so a tick never retries, releases or redispatches an item another session is working in its own clone; today selfcheck fails claims on two items a live operator-present session holds with a test run in progress, whose work commits sit in that session's worktree
notes: Theme: stale claims and a mixed fleet. Evidence: bl_stall.py:274-286 fires claim-no-commit on any claim older than CLAIM_NO_COMMIT_S with no work commit in this clone, whoever holds it; backlog.py selfcheck on 2026-10-04 failed claims on ST-tbi3rras and TK-fsvrji77, held by another session whose worker was running tests at that moment; kb-autopilot step 1 acts on each selfcheck failure, and the ladder's second remedy is release-redispatch. A parent story claimed while its task is worked shows the same signal.
